quests.instruction: It is pouring on a school morning, and Ravi usually walks. What is a sensible adjustment?
quests.correctAnswer: Take a Raincoat and Leave a Little Earlier 🌧️
options: Skip School Altogether Because of the Rain 🏠
Walk the Same Way as Usual with No Rain Gear 🚶
Take a Raincoat and Leave a Little Earlier 🌧️
quests.hint: Consider what the rain changes: the time needed and what to wear.
quests.explanation: Rain slows walking and soaks clothes, so leaving earlier with rain gear lets him arrive on time and dry. Ignoring it or skipping school does not help.
quests.funFact: Kerala receives around 3,000 millimetres of rain in a typical year, much of it in the monsoon.

quests.instruction: At break, the class usually plays football, but the field is waterlogged. What can they do?
quests.correctAnswer: Play an Indoor Game in the Hall 🎲
options: Play an Indoor Game in the Hall 🎲
Sit in Silence with Nothing to Do 😐
Play on the Waterlogged Field Anyway ⚽
quests.hint: Focus on keeping the break fun and safe.
quests.explanation: An indoor game keeps everyone active without slipping in mud. Playing in the water risks falls, and sitting silent wastes the break.
quests.funFact: Wet grass and mud are much more slippery than dry grass, which is why muddy fields are often closed.

quests.instruction: Dev usually cycles to the park after school, but a thunderstorm is forecast for the afternoon. What is a sensible change?
quests.correctAnswer: Plan Something Indoors Instead 🏠
options: Plan Something Indoors Instead 🏠
Go Anyway Without Telling Anyone 🚲
Cycle Early and Hope to Beat the Storm ⛈️
quests.hint: The clue is where it is safest during a storm.
quests.explanation: Staying indoors during a thunderstorm is safest, so he swaps the plan. Racing a storm or going without telling anyone is risky.
quests.funFact: Thunder is the sound of lightning heating the air so quickly that it expands with a boom.

quests.instruction: School starts an hour earlier tomorrow because of an exam. How should Anu adjust?
quests.correctAnswer: Go to Bed Earlier and Set the Alarm Earlier ⏰
options: Skip Breakfast and Brushing Her Teeth 🙈
Go to Bed Earlier and Set the Alarm Earlier ⏰
Wake at the Usual Time and Hurry Everything 🏃
quests.hint: The key is both ends of tonight's routine.
quests.explanation: Going to bed earlier keeps her rested, and an earlier alarm gives her time for her usual steps. Hurrying or skipping steps would leave her rushed and unprepared.
quests.funFact: Studies have found that students tend to do better on exams after a good night's sleep.

quests.instruction: PE has been moved from Tuesday to Wednesday this week. What should Mina change?
quests.correctAnswer: Pack Her PE Kit for Wednesday Instead 👟
options: Pack It for Tuesday as Usual This Week 📅
Pack Her PE Kit for Wednesday Instead 👟
Leave It at Home on Both Days 🏠
quests.hint: Think about which day the kit is needed now.
quests.explanation: The kit is needed on the new day, so she packs it for Wednesday. Packing for Tuesday would waste effort, and leaving it would mean missing PE.
quests.funFact: School timetables sometimes change for events such as sports days or exams.

quests.instruction: A substitute teacher takes the class and does things a little differently. What is a good way to adapt?
quests.correctAnswer: Listen to the New Teacher's Instructions 🙋
options: Do Nothing Until the Normal Teacher Returns 🕰️
Insist on the Usual Way 🙄
Listen to the New Teacher's Instructions 🙋
quests.hint: Think about who is in charge of the class today.
quests.explanation: The substitute is in charge today, so following their instructions keeps the class running. Insisting on the usual way or doing nothing causes problems.
quests.funFact: Substitute teachers are called supply or relief teachers in some countries.

quests.instruction: A picnic planned for Saturday has been moved to Sunday. What should Aanya do?
quests.correctAnswer: Check Her Other Plans for Sunday 📅
options: Go to the Park on Saturday Alone 🏞️
Cancel Everything and Be Upset 😠
Check Her Other Plans for Sunday 📅
quests.hint: Think about what the new day might clash with.
quests.explanation: Checking Sunday's plans shows whether anything clashes, so she can adjust. Going alone or cancelling everything would not help.
quests.funFact: Ancient civilisations such as the Babylonians and Egyptians made calendars to plan farming and festivals.

quests.instruction: A friend cannot come to play today, and Leo had been looking forward to it. What helps?
quests.correctAnswer: Find Another Activity or Call Another Friend 🧩
options: Find Another Activity or Call Another Friend 🧩
Sit and Complain All Afternoon 😠
Go to His Friend's House Without Telling Anyone 🚪
quests.hint: Focus on turning the plan into a new one.
quests.explanation: Having a back-up idea turns a disappointing change into something to look forward to. Complaining or turning up uninvited does not help.
quests.funFact: Spacecraft carry backup systems so that a single failure does not end the mission.

quests.instruction: The school play has been postponed by a week. What should Hari do about his rehearsals?
quests.correctAnswer: Keep Practising a Little So He Stays Ready 🎭
options: Practise Twice as Hard Every Day Until Then 📢
Stop Practising Altogether for the Week 🛑
Keep Practising a Little So He Stays Ready 🎭
quests.hint: Focus on keeping skills fresh without overdoing it.
quests.explanation: A little practice keeps the lines fresh without tiring him out. Stopping might mean forgetting, and doing twice as much is not needed.
quests.funFact: Short, regular practice usually helps memory more than occasional long sessions.

quests.instruction: Mum has already laid out Anu's uniform on her bed. What is the sensible next step?
quests.correctAnswer: Get Dressed and Move On to Breakfast 👕
options: Get Dressed and Move On to Breakfast 👕
Wait for Mum to Come and Dress Her 🕰️
Put It Away and Choose a New One 🗄️
quests.hint: Focus on not repeating a job that is already done.
quests.explanation: The uniform is ready, so she can use the time saved. Choosing again repeats work, and waiting for help she does not need wastes time.
quests.funFact: School uniforms are common in India and in many other countries, including the UK and Japan.

quests.instruction: Ravi finished his homework during a free period at school. What is a good way to use the evening?
quests.correctAnswer: Rest, Read or Play 📚
options: Make Up Extra Homework 📝
Rest, Read or Play 📚
Pretend He Still Has Homework 🙈
quests.hint: Consider what is left to do.
quests.explanation: With the homework finished, the evening can be used for rest or things he enjoys. Making up extra work or pretending is not needed.
quests.funFact: A school 'period' is a block of lesson time, often between 35 and 45 minutes long.

quests.instruction: Dia packed her bag last night, but this morning the teacher messages that a new book is needed. What is the best adjustment?
quests.correctAnswer: Add the New Book Without Repacking Everything 📘
options: Leave the New Book Out and Say Nothing 🤐
Add the New Book Without Repacking Everything 📘
Empty the Whole Bag Out and Start Over Again 🎒
quests.hint: The key is changing only what needs changing.
quests.explanation: Adding one book is quick, while repacking everything wastes time. Ignoring the message means she will not have what she needs.
quests.funFact: School diaries often have a page for notes between teachers and parents.

quests.instruction: It is nearly bedtime, and Priya has barely started her homework. What is a sensible choice?
quests.correctAnswer: Do What She Can and Tell the Teacher 🌙
options: Do What She Can and Tell the Teacher 🌙
Stay Up Past Midnight to Finish It All 🌌
Hide the Notebook and Say Nothing 🙈
quests.hint: Think about what matters more than finishing tonight.
quests.explanation: Sleep matters for tomorrow, so she does what she can and explains to the teacher. Staying up past midnight or hiding the work does not help.
quests.funFact: Sleeping after studying helps memories settle, so rested students often recall more.

quests.instruction: Bedtime is in fifteen minutes, but Leo's story takes twenty. What is the sensible choice?
quests.correctAnswer: Choose a Shorter Story Tonight 📖
options: Choose a Shorter Story Tonight 📖
Read the Long Story and Stay Up Late ⏰
Skip Brushing Teeth to Fit It In 🪥
quests.hint: Consider keeping the routine's most important parts.
quests.explanation: A shorter story fits the time and keeps bedtime on track. Staying up late or skipping teeth drops something important.
quests.funFact: Picture books are often 32 pages long, which takes about five minutes to read aloud.

quests.instruction: Tomorrow there is an early trip, so Mina must wake much earlier than usual. How can she adjust tonight?
quests.correctAnswer: Start Her Bedtime Routine Earlier 🌙
options: Skip the Routine Tonight 🚫
Keep the Usual Time and Wake Up Tired 😴
Start Her Bedtime Routine Earlier 🌙
quests.hint: Ask yourself how much sleep she still needs.
quests.explanation: Starting earlier lets her get enough sleep before the early wake-up. Keeping the usual time leaves her tired, and skipping the routine drops helpful steps.
quests.funFact: The body clock works best when sleep and wake times are fairly regular.

quests.instruction: Aarav wakes up with a stomach ache on a school day. What should he do?
quests.correctAnswer: Tell a Grown-up and Follow Their Advice 🧑
options: Tell a Grown-up but Ignore Their Advice 🏫
Take Some Medicine He Found at Home 💊
Tell a Grown-up and Follow Their Advice 🧑
quests.hint: Ask yourself who can decide what is best.
quests.explanation: A grown-up can decide whether he should rest, see a doctor or go to school, and he should follow their advice. Ignoring that advice or taking medicine on his own is unsafe.
quests.funFact: Stomach aches in children are often mild, but a grown-up should check, especially if there is a fever or the pain gets worse.

quests.instruction: Ila has a cold and is sneezing a lot. How should she adjust her day?
quests.correctAnswer: Rest, Drink Water and Wash Hands Often 💧
options: Hug Everyone Hello 🤗
Rest, Drink Water and Wash Hands Often 💧
Share Her Water Bottle with Friends 🧴
quests.hint: Focus on helping her body and protecting others.
quests.explanation: Rest and water help her recover, and washing hands stops germs spreading. Hugging or sharing bottles spreads the cold.
quests.funFact: Most colds are caused by viruses and go away on their own within about a week.

quests.instruction: After being ill for three days, Tara feels better but weak. How should she return to her routine?
quests.correctAnswer: Return Gradually and Rest When Needed 🌱
options: Return Gradually and Rest When Needed 🌱
Stay in Bed for Another Whole Week 🛏️
Do Everything at Full Speed Right Now 🏃
quests.hint: Think about how a body recovers.
quests.explanation: A gradual return lets her strength come back without a setback. Full speed may tire her, and staying in bed for a week is more than she needs.
quests.funFact: After an illness, energy usually comes back a little more each day.

quests.instruction: During the monsoon, the sky gets dark early in the evening. How might the family adapt after-school play?
quests.correctAnswer: Play Earlier and Come In Before Dark 🌆
options: Stop All Play for the Whole Season 🚫
Play Earlier and Come In Before Dark 🌆
Play Outside After Dark as Usual Anyway 🌙
quests.hint: Think about when there is the most light.
quests.explanation: Playing earlier makes use of the daylight, and coming in before dark keeps children safe. Playing after dark or stopping play are less helpful.
quests.funFact: Thick clouds can make evenings look darker earlier, even when sunset time has not changed.

quests.instruction: During the long summer holiday, there is no school. What is a sensible way to keep a routine?
quests.correctAnswer: Keep Fixed Points Like Meals and Bedtime 🕰️
options: Follow a Strict Timetable Every Minute 📋
Keep Fixed Points Like Meals and Bedtime 🕰️
Drop Every Routine for Weeks 🚫
quests.hint: Focus on keeping some structure without making it a chore.
quests.explanation: A few fixed points give the day shape without making it feel like school. Dropping all routines or planning every minute is hard to keep up.
quests.funFact: Keeping mealtimes and bedtimes steady helps the body clock, even when a holiday changes other things.

quests.instruction: Rohan starts in a new classroom at the beginning of the school year. What helps him settle in?
quests.correctAnswer: Learn the Layout and Ask Questions 🗺️
options: Stay Silent and Hope to Work It Out 🤐
Wait Until Someone Shows Him Everything 🕰️
Learn the Layout and Ask Questions 🗺️
quests.hint: Work out how to find out where things are.
quests.explanation: Looking around and asking questions helps him find where things go. Waiting or staying silent makes settling in slower.
quests.funFact: Most schools start the year with an orientation so that students can get familiar with the building.

quests.instruction: The family is on holiday in a hotel, and routines are looser. Which habits are still worth keeping?
quests.correctAnswer: Brushing Teeth and Drinking Enough Water 🪥
options: Brushing Teeth and Drinking Enough Water 🪥
Staying Up Until Dawn Every Night 🌙
Skipping Meals Altogether to Save Time 🍽️
quests.hint: The key is habits that look after the body wherever you are.
quests.explanation: Looking after teeth and staying hydrated matter in any place. Staying up all night or skipping meals does not help.
quests.funFact: Travellers often get thirsty without noticing, especially in hot weather or on planes.

quests.instruction: On a long journey the family eats at unusual times. What helps Dev?
quests.correctAnswer: Carry Healthy Snacks and Water 🍎
options: Eat Only Sweets 🍬
Wait Hungry Until the Next Stop 😖
Carry Healthy Snacks and Water 🍎
quests.hint: Think about keeping energy steady.
quests.explanation: Snacks and water keep energy steady between meals. Waiting hungry or eating only sweets leaves him tired or unwell.
quests.funFact: Dried fruit and nuts are popular travel snacks because they keep well without a fridge.

quests.instruction: On the first night in a new place, Dev wakes up and does not know where the bathroom is. What would have helped?
quests.correctAnswer: Ask Where It Is Before Bedtime 🚽
options: Wander Around the Dark Hotel Room 🏃
Ask Where It Is Before Bedtime 🚽
Hold It All Night Until Morning 😣
quests.hint: Decide what to find out before it gets dark.
quests.explanation: Finding out before bed means he can go safely at night. Wandering in the dark can cause falls, and holding it is uncomfortable.
quests.funFact: Night lights are used in many homes and hotels to help people find their way in the dark.

quests.instruction: Hari's mother is working late this week. How can he help the evening routine?
quests.correctAnswer: Do His Own Jobs and Help with a Small Task 🤝
options: Do His Own Jobs and Help with a Small Task 🤝
Wait for Mum to Get Home Before Doing Anything 🕰️
Skip Both Dinner and Homework 🙈
quests.hint: Ask yourself what he can take care of himself.
quests.explanation: Doing his own jobs and helping a little makes the evening smoother. Waiting for Mum or skipping dinner and homework adds problems.
quests.funFact: Families often share out evening jobs when someone is busy.

quests.instruction: A new baby has arrived, and the house is noisier. How can Priya adapt her homework routine?
quests.correctAnswer: Find a Quiet Spot or Study Earlier 🪑
options: Study Right Beside the Crying Baby 🍼
Give Up Homework for a Whole Month 🏳️
Find a Quiet Spot or Study Earlier 🪑
quests.hint: Decide when and where it is quietest.
quests.explanation: A quiet spot or an earlier time lets her concentrate. Giving up or working beside a crying baby does not help.
quests.funFact: Newborn babies sleep for many hours a day, but in short bursts.

quests.instruction: A grandparent has come to live with the family and rests in the afternoon. How should the children adapt their play?
quests.correctAnswer: Play Quietly Inside or Outdoors at That Time 🌳
options: Play Quietly Inside or Outdoors at That Time 🌳
Ask Grandparent to Rest Somewhere Else 🙄
Keep Playing Loudly Indoors Just as Before 🔊
quests.hint: Focus on respecting someone's rest.
quests.explanation: Quiet play or going outdoors lets the grandparent rest. Playing loudly or asking them to move is not considerate.
quests.funFact: Households where three generations live together are common in India.

quests.instruction: It is raining, school starts early and the bus is late. Which plan is best?
quests.correctAnswer: Leave Early with Rain Gear 🌧️
options: Stay Home and Tell Nobody 🏠
Leave Early with Rain Gear 🌧️
Ignore All the Changes 🙈
quests.hint: Decide what each change needs.
quests.explanation: Leaving early with rain gear covers the rain and the early start, and allows for the late bus. Ignoring everything or staying home without telling is no solution.
quests.funFact: Airlines advise passengers to arrive early, because check-in and security take time.

quests.instruction: Which is the best attitude when plans change?
quests.correctAnswer: Stay Calm, Look at Options, Choose the Best 🧠
options: Decide the Whole Day Is Ruined and Give Up 🏳️
Insist That Nothing at All Can Change 🔒
Stay Calm, Look at Options, Choose the Best 🧠
quests.hint: Remember what helps people solve problems.
quests.explanation: Staying calm lets you think clearly about options. Insisting nothing can change or giving up solves nothing.
quests.funFact: Pilots and sailors practise handling changes calmly because plans often change during a journey.

quests.instruction: A friend's birthday party is moved to the same time as Aman's swimming test. What should he do?
quests.correctAnswer: Talk to Both and Choose, Giving Notice Early 📞
options: Skip Both Without Saying Anything 🚫
Talk to Both and Choose, Giving Notice Early 📞
Go to the Party and Hope the Test Is Cancelled 🎈
quests.hint: The key is being honest and giving people time.
quests.explanation: Telling both and choosing early lets them adjust and keeps trust. Skipping both or hoping the test is cancelled is not fair.
quests.funFact: 'Notice' in this sense means formally telling someone about a change in advance, such as telling a landlord you are leaving.
